articles.title: Marimba: A System One Model for Speech. [R]
articles.summary: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18330 Follow-up to last week's post, now with the paper. You ask a typed question about an audio window (yes/no, a choice, or a score) and get a calibrated probability back. One frozen Qwen3-ASR-0.6B encoder pass per 8 s window serves all questions. How each question type is answered: - Term ("was 'satellite' said?"): zero-shot, scored from the decoder's greedy and 4 beam hypotheses, then Platt-calibrated. No training on the terms. - Language: the ASR model's own language scores. - Turn end: a small readout on frozen layer 18. - Speaker change and count: readouts on layer 12. Results: - On the same 1,000 public questions, it matches or beats Qwen3-Omni (30B-A3B) on 6 of 9 tests (image 1). Qwen3-Omni is still better on Speech Commands. Caveat: our turn-end readout was trained on Smart Turn data, so that row is in-distribution for us only. - Language ID: 100% on 300 FLEURS clips. - Speaker change AUROC 0.966-0.980 on AMI and VoxConverse, above ECAPA. articles.title: Role-Separated Diffusion Transformers: Global Rule Isolation and Deterministic Sampling Manifold Compression
articles.summary: We present Role-Separated Diffusion Transformers (RoSeDiT), a new diffusion transformer architecture that isolates the global rule from the image tokens. RoSeViT showed in visual reasoning that a vanilla ViT spreads a shared rule over all $L$ tokens at an entropy of order $Ld$, whereas an enforced controller route reduces it to order $d$. In class-conditional DiT and SiT, the class and the noise level are explicitly conditioned by adaLN, so a RoSeViT-style controller channel on the ViT side is insufficient to establish the full role separation. By introducing the adaLN listening mechanism, which makes adaLN compute under the controller's command, RoSeDiT brings the entropy theorem and role separation into the latent diffusion domain. Under the same SiT training and evaluation protocol at the same level of parameter count, RoSeDiT surpasses SiT at all four model scales at 400K steps, and RoSeDiT-L/2 even surpasses SiT-XL/2's 17.2 FID with 15.34 and 32% fewer parameters. articles.title: CISyn: Human Mesh Recovery in Close Interactions with Physics-Simulated Synthetic Data
articles.summary: 3D human mesh recovery (HMR) in close-interaction scenarios is hindered by the lack of large-scale, accurately annotated training data: real capture is expensive, and existing synthetic datasets rarely include physical contact. We introduce CISyn, a large-scale synthetic dataset purpose-built for close human-human interactions, generated via physics simulation and Blender-based rendering. By simulating collision dynamics between SMPL-X-rigged humanoids, CISyn naturally produces the contact, mutual occlusion, and pose entanglement that characterize close-interaction scenes, with no manual annotation effort. The released set provides 25,000 sequences with accurate 3D annotations. We further propose an uncertainty-aware loss that allows models to learn more effectively from the heavily occluded examples in our data. articles.title: DIRT: Depth-completed Image-based Rendering using Two-band Blending for Live Novel-view Synthesis
articles.summary: State-of-the-art novel-view synthesis (NVS) methods commonly require per-scene optimization before rendering, limiting their applicability in live settings. Live or ad-hoc NVS, however, demands low-latency rendering during capture and strong generalization to new scenes. Some previous work tried to address this task by adapting training- and optimization-based methods, trading quality for low latency. We introduce a live NVS approach following traditional image-based rendering that operates on a posed set of depth sensor observations and images. Our method leverages explicit, sparse point-based geometry obtained from active sensors, resulting in a sparsely filled depth buffer that is completed in the (novel) target view's screen-space. Using this proxy, a posed set of images is projected into the target frame before fusing the resulting observations through a frequency-aware two-band blending strategy. articles.title: Deep Bundle Adjustment
articles.summary: We present \textbf{DeepBA} (\textbf{Deep} \textbf{B}undle \textbf{A}djustment), a graph neural network (GNN) that recovers camera poses, intrinsics, and scene structure from 2D matches across an arbitrary number of views. Rather than solving a non-linear least-squares problem per scene, DeepBA amortizes bundle adjustment into a learned graph network that iteratively refines its estimate from geometric residuals. Where classical SfM computes its updates analytically and needs careful initialization, DeepBA learns them and converges from a cold start. It is trained with scale-invariant supervision (ground-truth rotation, translation direction, and intrinsics, plus reprojection self-consistency), so datasets with arbitrary metric units can be mixed without per-scene normalization. DeepBA is decoupled from the matcher.
